sub: Min, desired and max servers, kept healthy automatically.

Overview.p: An Auto Scaling Group (ASG) keeps the right number of EC2 instances running. You set minimum, desired and maximum size, a launch template and subnets in several AZs.
More customers, open more counters. Fewer customers, close some. If a counter breaks, it is replaced.
A ticket site runs 2 servers normally, grows to 10 when sales open, and drops back at night.

items: The ASG reads min, desired and max
It launches instances from the launch template
Bad ones are terminated and replaced

rows: Number the group tries to keep right now

items: Choose the VPC and 2 subnets in different AZs
Attach a load balancer target group (optional)
Create it and watch 2 instances launch
Terminate one instance by hand and watch the ASG replace it

Practical.p: Terminate or delete everything you created after practice to avoid charges.

items: Use an IAM instance profile in the template
Use a security group chain (ALB to instances)

Examples.p: Min 2 for availability, Max 10 for sales.

CLI Commands.p: IDs like i-0abc123 and sg-0abc123 are examples. Replace them with your real IDs.

items: Min is the floor, max is the ceiling, desired is the current target number.
If one AZ fails, instances in the other AZ keep serving.
What if an instance becomes unhealthy?
The ASG terminates it and launches a replacement.
The ASG changes the number of servers. The ELB shares traffic among them.
A wait time after a scaling action so the group does not scale again too fast.
Forgetting to delete the ASG after practice
